papers.title: Integrating emergency medicine-directed urgent care into a federally qualified health center: case report from a health professional shortage area.
papers.abstract: Underserved communities face significant barriers to healthcare access, often resulting in reliance on emergency departments (EDs) for non-emergent conditions. Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) play a key role in addressing these disparities, though many lack integrated urgent care services tailored to the needs of specific populations. This case study describes the implementation of an emergency medicine-directed urgent care department within an FQHC serving a predominantly Ultra-Orthodox Hasidic Jewish community in Kiryas Joel, New York. This report is intended as an implementation-focused description of how urgent care services can be integrated alongside primary care within an FQHC, rather than as a causal evaluation of ED use, clinical outcomes, or primary care utilization. A descriptive analysis of de-identified patient encounter data from 2020 to 2025 was conducted to characterize patient volume and utilization patterns. From 2020 to 2025, patient volume increased from 1,215 to 13,636 encounters, representing a 1022.3% increase. Pediatric patients accounted for 65.1% of visits, comprising the majority of encounters. The department provides extended hours, holiday accessibility, and integrated referral pathways, supporting high utilization in a community with significant cultural and linguistic barriers. This case study suggests that an emergency medicine-directed urgent care model can be successfully implemented within an FQHC and achieve high utilization in an underserved population. While causal impacts on emergency department utilization, primary care utilization, continuity of care, and clinical outcomes were not evaluated, this model offers a practical framework for health centers seeking to expand same-day urgent care access within an integrated FQHC setting.
papers.summary: 本研究探討將由急診醫學主導的緊急照護服務整合至聯邦合格健康中心（FQHC）的實施案例。該中心服務於紐約一個面臨顯著文化與語言障礙的極端正統猶太社區。數據顯示，從2020年至2025年，該緊急照護科的就診量從1,215次大幅成長至13,636次（增幅達1022.3%），其中兒科患者佔比高達65.1%。該模式透過提供延長時段、假日開放及整合轉診路徑，成功在醫療資源匱乏地區實現了高利用率。
papers.significance: 此案例研究為FQHC在資源不足及具有特殊文化語言需求的社區中擴展當日緊急照護提供了實用的實施框架。雖然本研究並未評估其對急診室利用率或臨床結果的因果影響，但其在醫療短缺地區所展現的驚人就診量成長證實了該模式的可行性，為未來基層醫療與緊急照護的深度整合發展提供了重要參考。
